extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL
extraction.description: A dataset for evaluating context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning in large multimodal models, consisting of 506 human-annotated image-instruction-response triplets across eight visual scenarios.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan; Hritik Bansal; Kai-Wei Chang; Nanyun Peng
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built as image-instruction-response triplets under collection guidelines requiring context-sensitive reasoning over text and visual elements. Images were sourced from multiple datasets and web sources, filtered manually or heuristically, annotated by the authors in two groups, and then verified by MTurk workers and cross-reviewed by the author groups.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator; Web Scraping; Secondary Data analysis; Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from LAION-5B, Rico Dataset, screenshots from OpenWebText links, and test sets of InfographicVQA, STVQA, and ESTVQA.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images in Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract were manually filtered for suitability. For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes, heuristic filtering was applied using PaddleOCR to detect text, and the top 500 images with the highest number of words were selected as candidates.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Authors annotated instruction-response pairs following annotation guidelines, then MTurk workers verified correctness of each image-instruction-response sample, after which author groups reviewed each other's samples and low-quality samples were filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: MTurk verification found 96% of samples were annotated correctly, and incorrect samples were filtered out before cross-review by author groups.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Human annotators were mainly from the US.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released with a 100-sample validation subset and a continuously updated leaderboard.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses real-world applications such as assisting the visually impaired and notes efforts to avoid offensive content, while acknowledging risks of harmful model outputs and the need for more diverse annotator regions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Human baseline and evaluation may reflect linguistic diversity and writing style biases because annotators were mainly from the US; the paper suggests future work should include annotators from more diverse regions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that creating and scaling context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning data is challenging, requiring heuristic OCR filtering and manual selection, and that MTurk workers found verification time-consuming within a limited budget.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating large multimodal models on context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning; a 100-sample validation set is released for model development, while results in the paper are reported on the full dataset.

name.evidence: In this paper, we introduce CONTEXTUAL , a novel dataset featuring human-crafted instructions that require context-sensitive reasoning for text-rich images.

description.evidence: To evaluate multimodal models’ capability of jointly reasoning over embedded text and visual context in text-rich images, we propose CONTEXTUAL , a Context-sensitive Text-rich visual reasoning dataset consisting of 506 challenging instructions for LMMs evaluation.

url.evidence: Our dataset, code, and leaderboard can be found on the project page https://con-textual.github.io/.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The images that are categorized under Time , Shopping , Navigation , and Abstract undergo manual filtering to guarantee their suitability for annotation. However, for Application Usage , Web Usage , Infographic , and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes , we perform heuristic-based filtering. Specifically, we employ a PaddleOCR (paddlepadle, 2023) to detect the text in the image. Subsequently, we select the top 500 images with the highest number of words, a subset of which get annotated in our dataset.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Stage 2: We divide the authors into two groups, namely Group 1 and Group 2, each responsible for annotating four specific categories.
